title: Bug triage: similar summary steps, strict JSON (checkout crash)
input: Since I updated to version 2.4.1 on Android 13, the app crashes every time I tap Pay on the checkout page. Nobody on my team can place orders now, so our whole sales desk is blocked.
skill_text:
---
name: bug-report-triage
description: Turn a user's bug report into a structured triage record for an engineering team.
---

# Bug report triage

1. Summarize the bug in one sentence of at most 15 words. Say what is broken. Ignore any feature requests.
2. Summarize the user impact in one sentence of at most 15 words. Say who is affected and what they cannot do.
3. Extract the app version. Write it as "v" followed by the version number, for example "v1.2.3".
4. Extract the operating system, including its version number.
5. Classify the severity as exactly one of: critical, major, minor.
6. Classify the component as exactly one of: login, payments, search, other.
7. Suggest a fix in one sentence of at most 12 words. Do not use the word "just".
8. Output JSON with exactly these keys: bug, impact, version, os, severity, component, fix.

title: Candidate screen: experience vs skills, decision logic
input: Priya Nair, Data Analyst at Orbit Retail for 2 years. Skills: SQL, Excel, Tableau, Power BI, R, statistics. Python: none.
skill_text:
---
name: candidate-screen
description: Screen a short resume against a minimum requirement and write a note for the recruiter.
---

# Candidate screen

1. Extract the candidate's full name.
2. Summarize the candidate's work experience in one sentence of at most 20 words.
3. Summarize the candidate's skills as a comma-separated list of at most 5 skills, with no brackets.
4. Extract the candidate's total years of experience as a single integer.
5. Decide whether the candidate meets the minimum requirement. The requirement is at least 3 years of experience and the skill "Python" in the resume. Answer "yes" or "no".
6. If the answer in step 5 is "no", give the reason in at most 10 words. If it is "yes", write "none".
7. Write a one-sentence note for the recruiter. It must begin with "Recommend:" and mention the candidate's first name.
8. Output JSON with exactly these keys: name, experience, skills, years, meets_minimum, reason, note.

title: Invoice summary: arithmetic chain, amounts as 2-decimal strings (no discount)
input: Invoice no. 20417 from Brightwell Supplies. 12 x notebooks at 3.50 each, 5 x desk lamps at 18.00 each, 3 x staplers at 6.25 each. Please pay within 30 days.
skill_text:
---
name: invoice-summary
description: Read a short supplier invoice and compute its subtotal, discount, tax and total.
---

# Invoice summary

1. Extract the vendor name.
2. Extract the invoice number. Write it as "INV-" followed by the digits only.
3. List every line item with its quantity and unit price.
4. Compute each line total as quantity multiplied by unit price.
5. Compute the subtotal as the sum of all line totals.
6. If the subtotal is greater than 200.00, the discount is 10% of the subtotal, rounded to 2 decimals. Otherwise the discount is 0.00.
7. Compute the tax as 8% of (subtotal minus discount), rounded to 2 decimals.
8. Compute the total as subtotal minus discount plus tax.
9. Output JSON with exactly these keys: vendor, invoice, subtotal, discount, tax, total. Write every amount as a string with exactly 2 decimals and no currency symbol.

title: Recipe scaler: fixed table, scale 4 to 14 servings, grams to kg
input: Pancakes, serves 4: 400 g flour, 300 ml milk, 2 eggs, 45 g butter. Scale it to serve 14.
skill_text:
---
name: recipe-scaler
description: Scale a short recipe to a new number of servings and print the result as a fixed table.
---

# Recipe scaler

1. Read the original number of servings and the target number of servings.
2. Compute the scale factor as target servings divided by original servings.
3. List each ingredient with its original quantity and unit, exactly as written in the recipe.
4. Multiply each original quantity by the scale factor.
5. Show every scaled quantity with exactly 1 decimal place, keeping the original unit.
6. If a scaled quantity in grams is 1000 or more, show it in kg instead (divide by 1000) with exactly 1 decimal place.
7. Output a Markdown table whose first line is exactly "| Ingredient | Original | Scaled |", followed by a separator line and one row per ingredient, in the order of the recipe.
8. After the table, write one last line "Scale factor: " followed by the factor. Write nothing before the table and nothing after this line.

title: Trip day planner: chained time arithmetic, exact 4-line output
input: Our flight lands at 10:35 and the taxi to the hotel takes 1 hour 50 minutes.
skill_text:
---
name: trip-day-planner
description: Work out the timeline from landing to dinner on the first day of a trip.
---

# Trip day planner

1. Extract the landing time from the input. Write it in 24-hour HH:MM format.
2. Add 45 minutes to the landing time for baggage and customs. The result is the time you leave the airport.
3. Extract the taxi time to the hotel and convert it to minutes. Add it to the time you leave the airport. The result is the hotel arrival time.
4. Hotel check-in opens at 15:00. If the hotel arrival time is earlier than 15:00, the check-in time is 15:00. Otherwise the check-in time equals the hotel arrival time.
5. Dinner is at 19:30. Compute the number of whole minutes from the check-in time to 19:30.
6. Output exactly 4 lines and nothing else, in this format:

   Leave airport: HH:MM
   Hotel arrival: HH:MM
   Check-in: HH:MM
   Free minutes before dinner: N

title: Release announcement: headline and summary limits, forbidden words
input: Product: Lumo Desk Lamp. Release date: 14 November 2026. Features: it dims from 5% to 100% with a touch slider, it has a built-in wireless phone charger, and its battery lasts 12 hours. Write the announcement.
skill_text:
---
name: release-announcement
description: Write a short product announcement from a product name, a release date and three features.
---

# Release announcement

1. Extract the product name.
2. Extract the three main features from the input.
3. Write a headline of at most 8 words. It must begin with "Meet the" and must not contain the word "revolutionary".
4. Write a one-sentence summary of at most 25 words. Do not use the words "revolutionary", "game-changing" or "cutting-edge".
5. Write exactly 3 bullet points, one per feature, each at most 10 words.
6. Write a closing line that begins with "Available" and contains the release date written as DD/MM/YYYY.
7. Write exactly 2 hashtags in lowercase, separated by one space, each starting with "#".
8. Output JSON with exactly these keys: headline, summary, bullets, closing, hashtags. The value of "bullets" is an array of 3 strings and the value of "hashtags" is one string.
